query: FeNiCrCoCu is considered promising for high-heat wear-resistant use and is suitable for thin-film applications; because bulk preparation is expensive, applying it as a coating on a conventional metal is more practical. Earlier studies reported improved wear or mechanical performance from high-entropy-alloy coatings on Al, Ni, and titanium-alloy substrates, and simulations of FeNiCrCoCu on Cu indicated that sliding speed affects tangential and normal forces. Other work associated composition and grain size with changes in wear damage. However, most prior studies examined a limited operating regime or the properties of the alloys themselves rather than the overall wear resistance of coatings under varied thermal conditions. Subject to retaining FeNiCrCoCu as a coating on a Cu matrix, what single intervention could improve its overall wear resistance during sliding across varied thermal and contact regimes? Present one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its causal mechanism, the predicted outcome relative to an unchanged coating in matched tests, the boundaries within which it should hold, supporting evidence from the introduction, and an experiment with a clear rejection criterion for both the predicted outcome and the proposed mechanism.

generation.hypothesis: The addition of Cr to the FeNiCrCoCu coating on a Cu matrix will improve its overall wear resistance during sliding across varied thermal and contact regimes.
generation.material_initial_state: FeNiCrCoCu coating on a Cu matrix
generation.intervention: Addition of Cr to the FeNiCrCoCu coating
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a BCC solid-solution phase and precipitation of the Laves phase
generation.mechanism: The addition of Cr refines the coating grains, promotes the precipitation of the Laves phase, and improves the hardness and high-temperature oxidation resistance of the coating, leading to improved wear resistance.
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved wear resistance of the FeNiCrCoCu coating with added Cr compared to the unchanged coating in matched tests
generation.baseline: FeNiCrCoCu coating on a Cu matrix without added Cr
generation.boundary: The improvement in wear resistance will be most significant at high temperatures and under conditions where oxidation resistance is crucial
generation.uncertainty: The optimal amount of Cr to be added and the specific effects of Cr on the microstructure and properties of the FeNiCrCoCu coating are uncertain

falsification_experiment.design: Compare the wear resistance of FeNiCrCoCu coatings with and without added Cr on a Cu matrix under varied thermal and contact regimes
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the wear resistance of the FeNiCrCoCu coating with added Cr is not significantly improved compared to the unchanged coating, the hypothesis is falsified

cited_evidence.text: Abstract WVTaTiCr x ( x = 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1) refractory high-entropy alloy coatings were prepared on a 42-CrMo steel plate using laser cladding. The purpose of this work is to investigate the effect of the Cr content on the microstructure and properties of the WVTaTiCr x coating. The morphologies and phase compositions of five coatings with different Cr contents were comparatively observed. In addition, the hardness and high-temperature oxidation resistance of the coatings were also analyzed. As a result, with the increase in Cr, the coating grains were more refined. All the coating is mainly composed of the BCC solid-solution phase, which promotes the precipitation of the Laves phase with the increase in Cr. The addition of Cr greatly improves the hardness, high-temperature oxidation resistance and corrosion resistance of the coating. The WVTaTiCr (Cr 1 ) exhibited superior mechanical properties, especially in terms of its exceptional hardness, high-temperature oxidation resistance and outstanding corrosion resistance. The average hardness of the WVTaTiCr alloy coating reaches 627.36 HV. After 50 h of high-temperature oxidation, the oxide weight of WVTaTiCr increases by 5.12 m

High-entropy alloys (HEAs) present a new approach of alloying concepts. Whereas conventional alloys usually comprise one major alloying element and minor additions of other alloying elements to improve properties, HEAs consist of at least five elements with close to equimolar composition. For several compositions, the desired formation of solely solid solutions with a face-centred cubic (fcc) or a body-centred cubic (bcc) structure could be achieved [ [1] , [2] , [3] ].

Several groups of HEAs have been intensively investigated. The term compositionally complex alloys (CCAs) was introduced for HEAs with a multiphase microstructure [ [4] ]. Several investigations prove the formation of primarily cubic phases in the alloy AlCoCrCuFeNi and its derivatives [ [5] , [6] , [7] ]. Aluminium strongly influences the microstructure, phase formation and resulting properties. Furthermore, aluminium acts as a stabiliser of bcc solid solutions and can suppress the formation of complex phases [ [8] , [9] , [10] ].
